correctness.rationale: A vertex outside a subset in a bipartite Fano incidence graph has at most one selected neighbor precisely if every selected point pair forces its joining line and every selected line pair forces their intersection point. The Fano axioms classify the selected point sets X into 0,1,2, collinear/noncollinear 3, four consisting of a line and exterior point, the full 7, with no other feasible larger proper X. For each class, the permitted Y are enumerated by mutually incident pencils/mandatory joining lines, yielding all displayed bivariate coefficients. Inclusion maximality then leaves exactly 21 (3,3) line-pencil flags and 28 (4,4) line-plus-exterior point configurations. Independently checking every one of 2^14=16384 subsets by the outsider-neighborhood condition produced exactly 366 convex sets, all bivariate coefficients and 49 proper maximal sets, matching the structural proof.

value.rationale: The Fano plane is the smallest projective plane and its Levi graph the canonical Heawood graph. A complete, geometrically explained P_3-convex lattice, bivariate profile and maximal proper configurations form a meaningful exact structural example of an algorithmically studied convexity notion; it is not a random tiny graph number. The result is appropriately limited to this natural fixed object.

final_claim: The bivariate P_3-convex-set enumerator of the Fano-plane incidence Heawood graph is the explicitly stated 14-vertex polynomial with total 366; 49 inclusion-maximal proper convex sets comprise 21 three-point/three-line flags and 28 four-point/four-line configurations; proper convex-set sizes avoid 7 and 9 through 13.
limitations: Exact fixed-graph classification; no extension to larger projective planes.
A generally available algorithm does not itself constitute this explicit table.
